items.q: In the provided ocular and orbital anatomy diagram, which structure passes OUTSIDE the common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn) through the superior orbital fissure?
items.exp: Structures passing outside the common tendinous ring through the superior orbital fissure include the Frontal nerve, Lacrimal nerve, Trochlear nerve (CN IV), and Superior ophthalmic vein. In contrast, the oculomotor nerve divisions, nasociliary nerve, and abducens nerve pass inside the ring.
r: Incorrect. The abducens nerve passes inside the tendinous ring.
Correct. The trochlear nerve passes outside the common tendinous ring with the frontal and lacrimal nerves.
Incorrect. The nasociliary nerve passes inside the tendinous ring.
Incorrect. Both divisions of CN III pass inside the tendinous ring.
items.kp: Trochlear, frontal, lacrimal nerves and superior ophthalmic vein pass OUTSIDE the common tendinous ring.

x.key: Trochlear, frontal, lacrimal nerves and superior ophthalmic vein pass OUTSIDE the common tendinous ring.
x.pearl: Trochlear, frontal, lacrimal nerves and superior ophthalmic vein pass OUTSIDE the common tendinous ring.

items.q: A 45-year-old patient undergoes an orbital floor reconstruction following a blowout fracture. Postoperatively, numbness is noted over the ipsilateral cheek, upper lip, and upper gingiva. Which nerve was injured within the orbital floor?
items.exp: The infraorbital nerve (branch of maxillary nerve V2) courses through the infraorbital groove and canal in the orbital floor before exiting onto the face via the infraorbital foramen. Blowout fractures commonly injure this nerve, causing paresthesia of the ipsilateral cheek, upper lip and anterior teeth.
r: Incorrect. Zygomaticotemporal nerve supplies temple skin.
Correct. The infraorbital nerve runs in the orbital floor and supplies the cheek and upper lip.
Incorrect. Lacrimal nerve runs along the upper lateral orbital wall.
Incorrect. Anterior ethmoidal nerve traverses the medial orbital wall.
items.kp: Infraorbital nerve runs along the orbital floor and is frequently damaged in maxillary blowout fractures.

x.key: Infraorbital nerve runs along the orbital floor and is frequently damaged in maxillary blowout fractures.
